static_findings.snippet: Add custom theme variables in your global.css using `@theme`:
4. **Theme config** - Use `@theme` in CSS instead of `tailwind.config.js`
5. **Component wrappers** - Must wrap components with `useCssElement` for className support
6. **Metro config** - Use `withNativewind` with different options (`inlineVariables: false`)
2. Check that components are wrapped with `useCssElement`
- autoprefixer is not needed in Expo because of lightningcss

content.value_statement: Expo teams need consistent styling across native and web targets. This skill gives a focused setup path for Tailwind CSS v4, NativeWind v5, and react-native-css.
actual_capabilities: Shows the Expo install command for Tailwind CSS v4, NativeWind v5, react-native-css, and related utilities.
Provides Metro and PostCSS configuration examples for the NativeWind v5 setup.
Defines CSS-enabled wrappers for View, Text, ScrollView, Pressable, TextInput, Image, and animated components.
Explains Tailwind v4 CSS-first theme variables and platform media queries for iOS, Android, and web.
Documents migration differences from NativeWind v4 and Tailwind CSS v3.
Includes troubleshooting checks for missing styles, platform colors, and TypeScript className props.
limitations: The guidance targets Tailwind CSS v4 and NativeWind v5 preview packages, so package APIs may change.
It does not generate files automatically; users or agents must apply the examples to the project.
It assumes an Expo project with compatible React Native dependencies already exists.
It does not validate visual output on devices or simulators.

use_cases.title: Set Up a New Expo App
use_cases.description: Add Tailwind CSS v4 styling support to a new Expo project with native and web targets.

use_cases.title: Migrate Styling Configuration
use_cases.description: Replace older NativeWind and Tailwind configuration patterns with the CSS-first v4 approach.

use_cases.title: Standardize Component Styling
use_cases.description: Create shared CSS-enabled components so app screens can use className consistently.

prompt_templates.title: Install Tailwind Dependencies
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup in an existing Expo app
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to list the packages and configuration files needed for Tailwind CSS v4 in my Expo project.

prompt_templates.title: Create Expo Config Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the Expo Tailwind setup guidance to create or update my Metro config, PostCSS config, and global CSS file.

prompt_templates.title: Build CSS Wrapper Components
prompt_templates.scenario: Enable className on React Native components
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add reusable CSS-enabled wrappers for core React Native components in my Expo app.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a NativeWind Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration from older styling setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current Expo styling setup and use this skill to plan a migration from NativeWind v4 or Tailwind v3 to the v5 and v4 stack.

output_examples.input: I need Tailwind CSS v4 in an Expo app that targets iOS, Android, and web.
output_examples.output: A setup plan covering package installation, Metro configuration, PostCSS configuration, global CSS imports, and shared className wrappers.

output_examples.input: My NativeWind styles are not applying after migration.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist for CSS imports, NativeWind Metro integration, wrapped components, and TypeScript className props.

output_examples.input: I want iOS semantic colors in Tailwind utilities.
output_examples.output: Guidance for defining CSS variables, using platform media queries, and registering colors in the Tailwind theme layer.

best_practices: Start with the Metro, PostCSS, and global CSS configuration before adding component wrappers.
Keep CSS-enabled component wrappers in one shared directory for consistent imports.
Test styling on iOS, Android, and web because platform media queries can resolve differently.
anti_patterns: Do not keep an old NativeWind Babel preset when using the v5 Metro transformer approach.
Do not use unwrapped React Native primitives when className support is required.
Do not assume Tailwind v3 configuration files apply unchanged to Tailwind CSS v4.

faq.question: Does this skill create files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup guidance and examples that an agent or developer can apply to an Expo project.

faq.question: Which Tailwind version does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Tailwind CSS v4 with the CSS-first configuration model.

faq.question: Does it require a Babel config?
faq.answer: No. The guide states that NativeWind v5 uses Metro configuration instead of a Tailwind Babel preset.

faq.question: Can it support web and native platforms?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples cover iOS, Android, and web styling patterns through Expo and CSS media queries.

faq.question: Is NativeWind v5 stable?
faq.answer: The skill references a preview release, so users should verify current package compatibility before production use.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
